$comment: Public repositories at the commit before they upgraded @prisma/client from >=6 <7 to >=7 <8, and every finding the pack must report there. See docs/packs.md, "Ground truth". Drafted with packs:truth; the lines the upgrade changed in schema.prisma, package.json and prisma.config.* were read from the same `git diff -U0` by hand (packs:truth lists source files and tsconfigs only), with the same rules. The compiler draft is never a site here: with @prisma/client 7 linked next to a client generated at 6 it reports TS2305/TS7006/TS7031/TS2339 that a real upgrade, which regenerates the client, never has (RESEARCH.md).

repos.why: A TanStack Start app already on the prisma-client generator: the datasource URL moves to prisma.config.ts, the client gets the pg adapter, and the CLI scripts load .env with dotenv-cli and run generate themselves. The vite plugin that copied the engine binaries (removed in 7) and the @@map reordering are cleanup, not sites.

findings.note: anchor: adapter added to the constructor options
db:push now runs gen:prisma after the push

repos.why: A Next.js app on prisma-client-js: the smallest real upgrade, the schema URL and one client with the pg adapter.

findings.note: anchor: adapter added to the constructor options

repos.why: A Next.js pages app with a client per API route, all without options: each throws at construction on 7. It also moved the seed out of package.json and switched to the prisma-client generator (better-sqlite3 adapter). The import and jest mock changes follow the generator switch and are not sites.

findings.note: lines 7-8 were only rewrapped into createPrismaClient(), the repository's own refactor

repos.why: An Express API: datasourceUrl becomes the pg adapter, connection_limit moves from the URL to the pool's max, the schema path leaves package.json. It also switched to the prisma-client generator; the Prisma.dmmf, Prisma.validator and import rewrites follow that switch (prisma-client-js 7 still has them), and the reporting SQL changes are unrelated.

findings.note: &connection_limit= dropped from the URL, max set on the adapter

repos.why: A framework monorepo whose integration harness (apps/pg-integration) loads the generated client with a dynamic import: the clients get the pg adapter, and db:push loses --skip-generate. Scored from the root: its lockfile is there. The hand-typed constructor signatures it widened (new () => to new (opts?) =>) follow its own fix and are not sites. The reference schemas under packages/*-prisma, which no workspace with @prisma/client loads, did not change.

An npm-workspaces monorepo whose API tests point clients at other databases with datasources: each becomes the pg adapter. prisma.config.ts existed on 6 (the datasource it gained is the schema URL moving, not a site of its own). The Node engines bump and the ?schema= handling are the repository's choice; no source covers the latter.

repos.withoutGenerated: backend/prisma.config.ts reads env("DATABASE_URL"), which throws when the variable is unset: prisma generate needs the project's database URL at this commit.
repos.why: A NestJS backend already on prisma-client and prisma.config.ts: engine "classic" leaves the config (TS2353 at 7), the seed moves out of package.json, the clients get the pg adapter. PrismaService (extends PrismaClient) gained a constructor: an insertion into a class body, which the ground-truth rules do not count as a site.

findings.note: line 107 only loses the comma before the removed key
